name: FileViewer html preview
description:
1. Task: add an HTML "preview" mode to the `FileViewer` component, showing `.html`/`.htm` files rendered by default.
2. Solution: extended the existing `viewMode` switcher pattern (already used for `.canva`) into a "Preview / Code" toggle in the header.
3. Implementation: added `isHtml`, `hasViewSwitcher`, `isPrimaryViewMode`, `isHtmlPreviewMode` plus dynamic label/icon/title helpers, and an `HTML_EXTENSIONS` constant.
4. Rendering: a sandboxed `<iframe :srcdoc="fileContent">` for the live preview, with `VueCodeHighlighter` showing the source in Code mode.
5. Canva's editable Save/Discard flow stayed untouched, and the known limitation is that relative asset paths don't resolve inside `srcdoc`.

messages.content: Add html files "preview" mode in the FileViewer component

I'll explore the project to find the FileViewer component and related files.Let me read the full FileViewer component and the existing HTMLPreview component.Let me inspect the file API helpers to understand how preview URLs work.I have everything needed. The request targets `src/components/filebrowser/FileViewer.vue`, which already implements a "switcher" pattern (`viewMode: 'editor' | 'content'`) for canva files. I'll extend that same pattern to HTML files with a **Preview / Code** toggle, reusing the existing header switcher and chrome. ## Change summary | File | Change | |---|---| | `src/components/filebrowser/FileViewer.vue` | Add `isHtml` detection, generalize the editor/content switcher into a **Preview / Code** switcher for `.html`/`.htm` files, and render a sandboxed live `

## Design notes - **Default view = Preview.** HTML files open rendered (like images/PDFs), matching the "preview mode" intent. Users flip to **Code** when they need the source. - **Consistent chrome:** the toggle reuses the existing DaisyUI `join`/`btn-xs` component pattern — same hit area, focus behavior, and `btn-primary` active state as the canva switcher. - **Semantic labels per file type:** "Preview / Code" (HTML) vs. "Editor / Content" (canva) avoids ambiguity. - **No false "unsaved changes":** `isContentMode` stays canva-only, so the HTML source view (read-only highlighter) never shows Save/Discard badges. - **Accessibility:** the switcher buttons carry `title` tooltips and reuse visible `i` icons (no color-only state); the iframe has a descriptive `title`. ### Anti-patterns avoided - ❌ Reusing `HTMLPreview.vue` (it injects its own dark body styles/padding, which would **override the actual document** being previewed). - ❌ Making the source view editable for HTML (would need a separate staging flow and would mislead with Save prompts). - ❌ Un-sandboxed `
